Chapter 16The economics

The Economics of AI Chips

Epoch AI estimated in December 2025 that Nvidia's B200 AI chip cost about $6,400 to build, mostly for memory and packaging. Its processor silicon cost about $900.

2,125 words / 9 minSpecimen: wafer costUpdated 25 October 202633 sources

Cite this chapter·Chapter PDF

In plain terms

Most of what it costs to build Nvidia's B200, an AI chip from its Blackwell line, goes to memory and packaging that a few firms supply. A bill of materials is the list of parts inside a product and what each one costs. Epoch AI estimated in December 2025 that the B200 cost about $6,400 to build[1]. The two logic dies, the pieces of silicon that do the calculating, cost about $900 of that[1]. The stacked memory beside them accounted for about half, and the packaging that wires the dies and memory together cost more than the dies[1]. Three firms, SK hynix, Samsung and Micron, dominate the world market for that memory[2]. One Taiwanese firm, TSMC, does that packaging[1].

In short

Epoch AI says Nvidia's margin on Blackwell may be lower than the gap between the B200's build cost and its selling price suggests[1]. It cites reports from March 2024 that put the B200's selling price at $30,000 to $40,000 per chip[1]. Epoch AI notes that most Blackwell revenue comes from servers and rack-scale systems, which may carry lower margins[1].

In 2026 Micron's gross margin, the share of sales left after production costs, passed Nvidia's. Micron's rose from 39.8 percent for the year to August 2025 to 80.7 percent for the year to September 2026[3]. It reached 86.8 percent in the last quarter of that year[3]. Nvidia's was 75.0 percent in the quarter to July 2026[4]. Epoch AI's estimate priced memory at $14 to $17 per gigabyte, before the 2026 rise in memory makers' sales and margins[5].

A B200, one of Nvidia's Blackwell AI chips, sells for far more than it costs to build. In December 2025 Epoch AI estimated that building one cost about $6,400[1]. Epoch AI cites reports from March 2024 that put its selling price at $30,000 to $40,000 per chip[1]. Most B200s are sold inside Nvidia's GB200 rack systems[6]. Epoch AI's chip sales model, with data through October 2025, puts what Nvidia earns per GPU for the computing hardware in those racks at $33,000 to $42,000[6]. That figure leaves out the networking gear in the racks[6].

How it works

Three numbers set the cost of a die, the finished rectangle of circuitry cut out of a wafer.

  • Wafer price. TSMC does not publish it. TSMC makes Nvidia's Blackwell chips on a custom-built process called 4NP[7]. Epoch AI estimates $17,000 for a 12-inch (300 mm) wafer on that process[1].
  • Dies per wafer. A wafer is a circle and dies are rectangles, so the edge of the wafer goes to waste. The bigger the die, the fewer fit. Each of the two logic dies in a B200 is about 800 mm2[1]. Nvidia calls them reticle-limited, meaning they are near the largest size a scanner can print in one shot[7].
  • Yield. Yield is the share of dies that work. Defects land at random, so a bigger die is more likely to catch one. Epoch AI models Blackwell die yield at 40 to 70 percent, centered on 60[1].

Together, those three numbers put the two dies inside a B200 at about $900[1]. Epoch AI's estimate for the whole B200 counts only variable costs, which rise with each chip made[1]. It leaves out fixed costs such as research and development[1].

Variants and trade-offs

Memory is the largest line

The largest line on the bill is the 192 GB of high-bandwidth memory beside those dies, a generation called HBM3E[1]. At $14 to $17 per gigabyte it comes to about $2,900, which Epoch AI counts as half of the build cost[1]. Epoch AI says HBM prices are negotiated deal by deal and can vary significantly with volume and contract length[1]. The $14 to $17 range dates from December 2025, before the 2026 rise in memory makers' sales and margins described below[5]. SK hynix said DRAM and NAND flash prices rose significantly in the second quarter of 2026 from the quarter before, led by high-performance products for AI servers[5].

Few firms make this memory, and one of them says demand has outrun its supply. SK hynix, Samsung and Micron dominate the world market for it[2]. SK hynix said in July 2026 that demand for its products had exceeded its available supply in recent quarters[8].

Packaging, substrate and test

CoWoS-L, the TSMC process that mounts dies and memory on one carrier and wires them together, adds about $1,100, more than the logic dies it carries[1]. Epoch AI models packaging yield at 65 to 95 percent[1]. A package that fails testing loses its logic dies and memory stacks[1]. Spreading that loss over the good units adds about $1,000 to each B200[1]. Power delivery hardware, the circuit board, and final assembly and testing add $480[1]. See Advanced packaging for how tight packaging capacity has been.

Epoch AI models each line as a range, deriving the packaging line from TSMC's advanced packaging revenue and Nvidia's share of CoWoS capacity[1].

Epoch AI says Nvidia's actual margin on Blackwell may be lower than the gap between the B200's build cost and its reported chip price suggests[1]. The estimate covers the accelerator module only and leaves out servers and rack-scale systems[1]. Epoch AI notes that most Blackwell revenue comes from those systems, which may carry lower margins[1].

Epoch AI's line-by-line estimate covers the B200, which is no longer Nvidia's newest chip. In its results for the quarter to July 2026, Nvidia said its Vera Rubin platform was ramping into full production[4]. Each Rubin GPU carries up to 288 GB of HBM4, a newer generation of the stacked memory[9].

From package to rack to cluster

Each new generation of Nvidia rack costs its owner more per hour than the last[10]. At rack scale, cost is measured per GPU-hour, one GPU running for one hour. For an operator that owns the machine, SemiAnalysis put a Vera Rubin NVL72 at $3.57 per GPU-hour in July 2026, against $1.84 for a GB200 and $2.36 for a GB300[10].

But SemiAnalysis found Rubin cheaper than GB200 and GB300 per token, a short chunk of text[10]. Rubin stayed cheaper at every level of interactivity SemiAnalysis compared, where interactivity is the number of tokens per second each user receives[10]. That finding rests on early results from the cloud provider CoreWeave running the DeepSeek R1 model, and SemiAnalysis said it had not verified them[10].

One level up, a cluster needs power and a network as well as servers. SemiAnalysis estimated in June 2024 that a cluster of 100,000 of Nvidia's earlier H100 GPUs cost over $4 billion in servers[11]. The cluster needs more than 150 MW of data center capacity and uses 1.59 TWh a year, which costs $123.9 million at $0.078 per kWh[11]. In the network design Nvidia recommended, 98,304 optical transceivers link the cluster's GPUs to the first layer of switches, called leaf switches[11].

Who captures the value

FirmStageQuarter endedGross margin
MicronHBM and DRAMSeptember 202686.8%[3]
NvidiaAccelerator designJuly 202675.0%[4]
TSMCWafers and CoWoSSeptember 202666.4%[12]
KLA (non‑GAAP)InspectionJune 202662.4%[13]
ASMLLithographySeptember 202657.5%[14]
Lam ResearchEtchJune 202651.7%[15]

In the table, gross margin is highest at the memory maker Micron and lowest in assembly and test. The firms in design, equipment and leading-edge wafers earn gross margins of 50.3 to 75.0 percent, and those in assembly and test 16.8 to 27.3 percent. Micron's gross margin rose from 39.8 percent for the year to August 2025 to 80.7 percent for the year to September 2026[3]. It reached 86.8 percent in the last quarter of that year[3].

Each figure except KLA's comes from the firm's own earnings release. KLA's shareholder letter gives only a non-GAAP gross margin for the quarter, 62.4 percent[13]. KLA's non-GAAP figures adjust its results under US accounting rules, known as GAAP, to leave out items such as acquisition-related charges and restructuring, severance and other charges[19]. For ASE the table shows its packaging and test segment[17]. The company as a whole had a gross margin of 21.0 percent, because about a third of its revenue came from electronics manufacturing services, which earned 8.9 percent[17].

The table leaves out two firms whose results give no gross margin. SK hynix's operating margin was 76 percent in the quarter to June 2026, and its revenue was up 257 percent from a year earlier[5]. The substrate maker Ibiden's operating profit was 21.8 percent of net sales in the quarter to June 2026[20].

World chip sales are forecast to jump in 2026, with memory growing far faster than logic. The Semiconductor Industry Association, using monthly data compiled by World Semiconductor Trade Statistics, counted $791.7 billion of global chip sales in 2025[21]. In its June 2026 forecast, World Semiconductor Trade Statistics put 2025 slightly higher, at $795.6 billion[22]. It forecast $1.51 trillion for 2026, with memory growing about 250 percent and logic 37 percent[22].

In 2025 capital spending at five large tech firms far exceeded the world's sales of chipmaking equipment. The industry group SEMI counted $135.1 billion of semiconductor equipment billings in 2025[23]. Capital spending at Alphabet, Amazon, Meta, Microsoft and Oracle came to $448.2 billion in 2025, the sum of Epoch AI's quarterly figures[24]. Epoch AI says that spending would reach $770 billion in 2026 if the trend continues[24]. These totals overlap, so they cannot be added together.

Where the money goes

The table below sorts each stage by whether its cost falls as volume grows. A structurally expensive stage stays costly because the work is hard, capacity is short or one firm sets the price. A stage compressible with scale gets cheaper as volume grows. An already commoditized stage has several competing suppliers. The classes are a judgment drawn from the sources in this chapter and the stage chapters.

StageClassWhy
EUV lithographyStructurally expensiveOne supplier, ASML. See Lithography.
Masks and pelliclesStructurally expensiveEvery design needs its own mask set, and every EUV layer a flawless mask. See Photomasks and pellicles.
Metrology and inspectionStructurally expensiveKLA held 56.8 percent of the market for these tools in 2025, by CSET's analysis of TechInsights data[25]. See Metrology and inspection.
HBMStructurally expensiveSK hynix says HBM needs more wafer input than ordinary DRAM[8]. See Memory and HBM.
Advanced packaging, CoWoS-LStructurally expensiveModeled packaging yield is 65 to 95 percent, and a failed package loses its dies and memory.
ABF substratesStructurally expensiveInvestment can add substrate lines, but Ajinomoto said in June 2026 that the insulating film it makes for these substrates has held over 95 percent of its market since launch[26]. See Substrates and PCBs.
Power and cooling plantStructurally expensiveIn the United States, grid connections face long queues, so at least three of OpenAI's seven Stargate sites will use on-site natural gas plants[27]. GE Vernova's backlog of gas power equipment, together with agreements reserving future production slots, grew from 100 GW to 116 GW in the second quarter of 2026[28]. See Data centers and power.
Optical transceiversStructurally expensiveIn May 2026 Nikkei reported that building AI data centers had caused shortages and price rises for lasers, optical fibers and other optical parts[29]. Nvidia agreed in March 2026 to invest $2 billion in the laser maker Lumentum, with rights to future capacity[30]. It agreed a similar $2 billion deal with Coherent[31]. See Systems and networking.
Leading-edge logic wafersCompressible with scaleA very large die yields well only once a process matures. See Transistors and the front end.
Design and EDACompressible with scaleA design is paid for once, and its cost is spread across every chip sold. See Chip design, EDA and IP.
Deposition and etch toolsCompressible with scaleMost deposition and etch steps have three or four established tool makers. See Deposition and etch.
Test and assembly (OSAT)Already commoditizedGross margins of 16.8 to 27.3 percent at Amkor and ASE's packaging and test segment, in the table above.
Wafers and bulk gasesAlready commoditizedSeveral firms make approved 300 mm wafers. By Siltronic's estimate, the five largest wafer makers served around 75 percent of the market in the first three quarters of 2025[32]. See Silicon and wafers.
Rack integration (ODM)Already commoditizedIn October 2025 Nvidia said more than 50 makers of systems and components were gearing up for the Vera Rubin NVL72[33]. See Systems and networking.

Review questions

Open a question to see its answer.

What does an Nvidia B200 cost to build?

About $6,400, in Epoch AI's December 2025 estimate.

Reports in March 2024 put its selling price at $30,000 to $40,000 per chip. Epoch AI says Nvidia's margin may be lower than that gap suggests, because most Blackwell revenue comes from servers and racks, which may carry lower margins. Reread: The B200 bill of materials

What is the most expensive part of an Nvidia B200?

The stacked memory, about $2,900 in Epoch AI's December 2025 estimate, or about half of the cost to build.

The two logic chips that do the calculating cost about $900. Reread: Memory is the largest line

Why does packaging add so much to the cost of a B200?

The CoWoS-L process itself costs about $1,100, more than the $900 logic chips, and a package that fails testing wastes the chips and memory inside it.

In Epoch AI's estimate, spreading the cost of those failed packages over the good ones adds about $1,000 to each B200. Reread: Packaging, substrate and test
